title: Research source catalog
description: Authoritative catalog of every source referenced by research reports. Top-level object is a map of {id -> record}. Each record's id is sha256(canonical_url)[:10]. Files for a record physically live at reference-only/<id>/<filename> unless files[].location overrides.

id.description: First 10 hex chars of sha256(canonical_url). Must match the parent map key.

pointer_to.description: If non-null, this record is superseded; canonical content lives at the pointed-to record. Use when we discover an earlier record had the wrong URL or when an upstream URL was renamed.

canonical_url.description: The URL whose sha256 prefix is this record's id. Required unless the record was created title-only (search hints set).

original_url.description: The pre-canonicalization URL if it differed from canonical_url. Useful for back-references from old links.

title.description: The source's own title, not the URL or filename. Use '(unknown)' if not yet determined.

short_summary.description: 8-10 word summary suitable for the markdown browse view.

long_summary.description: Paragraph-length summary of the source's content and relevance.

comments.description: Unstructured notes about the record itself (not file-specific; file-specific notes live in files[].comment).

search_hints.description: Free-form hints for locating the source. Each hint gets marked tried/found as it's exhausted.

references_from.description: Repo-relative paths of research reports that cite this source's canonical_url. Auto-derived by check-source-refs.

raw_bibtex.description: Escape hatch when structured fields don't fit (transcripts, blog posts, etc.).

files.description: Every physical file representing this source, OR file entries with ingestion_status=want representing desired formats not yet acquired.

format.description: MIME-style format identifier. 'other' for anything not in the enum. 'youtube-transcript' is a plain-text transcript of a YouTube video — the file's first line is the video URL; the rest is the transcript body. Requires the file entry to carry a `youtube_url` field.

filename.description: Basename only (no path). Default location is reference-only/<id>/<filename>. Null when ingestion_status=want and no specific filename is desired yet.

location.description: Override the default reference-only/<id>/<filename> path. Use for legacy files that live under reference-only/<topic>/ or for shared assets in research/figures/.

sha256.description: sha256 of the file content. Computed and stored when ingestion_status=have.

ingestion_status.description: have=file present on disk; want=we want this format/file but don't have it; skip-not-necessary=we have what we need in other formats; skip-unknown=we don't know if we want it.

completeness.description: complete=full content captured; partial=truncated/missing sections; error=fetch produced an error page (404, paywall, JS shell); unknown=not yet verified.

comment.description: File-specific notes. For images, this is where the image's auto-generated summary lives.

youtube_url.description: Only present (and required) when format="youtube-transcript". The URL of the YouTube video the transcript is for — recorded on the file entry rather than the parent record's canonical_url, because the parent record is the document where the video was embedded, not the video itself. When ingestion_status=have, the same URL must also appear as the first line of the transcript file.

fetch_provenance.description: When this file was acquired via the fetch-blocked-urls workflow, track the issue/PR/branch so linters can flag stale open work once the file is complete.
